slide.title: Close the books in [[5 days]] instead of 12

body.text: We standardize reconciliations, automate intercompany matching and move review earlier.

templates.name: Key message · statement

body.text: Review moves to the [[start]] of the close, not the end
Exceptions route to owners on day one, so day nine is for sign-off, not discovery.

templates.name: Narrative · lead and three points
templates.purpose: A short argument in prose at reading width: one lead sentence, three lead-in points.

slide.title: Three causes explain most of the delay

source.text: West Monroe close calendar analysis, FY26, 14 business units.

body.text: Close takes 12 days today. About 7 of them are spent waiting, not working.

items.text: Balance-sheet accounts are reconciled after close, not during the month.
Eleven entities match balances by email and spreadsheet.
Controllers see most entries for the first time on day nine.

templates.name: Cards · three columns
templates.purpose: Three parallel ideas as numbered cards with a Grounded Blue band.

slide.title: Three moves take the close from 12 days to 5

body.p: Map the close calendar for all 14 business units and rank each delay by days lost.
Move review to the start of the cycle and set the rules that check entries as they post.
Roll out in three waves, starting with the five entities that drive most of the delay.

templates.name: Cards · four columns
templates.purpose: Four short parallel ideas on subtle cards with inline numbers.

slide.title: Four steps, one owner for each

body.p: Rank every delay by the days it costs.
Move review to the start of the cycle.

body.text: We do not need faster spreadsheets. We need to stop finding problems on day nine.
